items.stem: Why do historians reject the claim that 'Africa had no history before European contact'?

options.text: Africa had many states, cities, trade networks and written and oral records long before contact
options.rationale: Correct: abundant evidence documents complex pre-contact African societies.

options.text: Because Africa was uninhabited until then
options.rationale: Africa is central to human origins and was long inhabited.
African societies kept oral and written records of their own.
There was extensive change; the myth erases it.

items.stem: A survey course covers Africa only through the Atlantic slave trade and colonialism. What is the historiographical problem?

options.text: It reduces a long, diverse history to episodes of external disruption and erases African agency
options.rationale: Correct: this framing omits deep history, states and internal dynamics, distorting the record.
They matter greatly; the problem is making them the whole story.

options.text: Africa has no other documented history
options.rationale: There is extensive other history to cover.

options.text: Slavery and colonialism had no lasting effects
options.rationale: They had major effects; the issue is exclusivity of focus.

items.explanation: Correct: this framing omits deep history, states and internal dynamics, distorting the record.
